parsed.main_gap: Lemma 4 falsely deduces from |E|<|V| that the whole multigraph is acyclic/loopless; only some component must be a tree, and it need not be the one containing vertex n.

errors.description: Graph-theoretic step in Lemma 4 is invalid: a multigraph with |E|<|V| can contain cycles/loops (e.g. a triangle plus isolated vertices); the stated justification ("a cycle through v vertices uses at least v edges, so |E|>=|V|") is wrong. The needed fact — that SOME component is a loopless tree — does follow, and since (3.1) holds for every nonempty index set the argument repairs in one line by taking any tree component instead of the one containing vertex n.
errors.quote: Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible.

parsed.notes: Correct answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1). Picking-phase lemma, geometric construction, and the pigeonhole + cross-pairing upper bound are all carefully and correctly done (I checked (2.1),(2.2), the mark count m-1=n, and the grid-matching claims). Only the acyclicity step is faulty.
